content:
The option "Edit as New Message" is only available when a user right-clicks on the body of an email.

There are other ways to do that. In the main Thunderbird window select the folder with the message in the folder pane. Select the message in the message pane. Press Alt or F10 to bring up the menu bar in case it is hidden. From the main menu bar: Message - Edit As New Message

Another way: Right-click the message in the message pane. From the drop-down menu select "Edit As New Message"

The option is also not available in the right-click menu on an email in a mailbox list.

It is, see above.

And yet another way: In the message window with the message open, select Message from the menu bar - Edit As New Message

content:
To have Thunderbird OAuth2 re-authenticate your account...

- Make sure that you have cookies enabled in Thunderbird (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Accept cookies from sites>;

- Delete any saved cookies for Yahoo (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Show Cookies>);

- Remove any existing entries for this account in Saved Passwords (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Passwords | Saved Passwords>);

- Restart Thunderbird, after which you should be prompted to re-authenticate.

I'm somewhat skeptical that this will solve the problem. Usually you would see authentication errors in that situation, not "security" and "certificate" errors.

What anti-virus/security software do you use, if any? Have you tried disabling it?
